A1.justification: Both complete, readable 20-page PDFs describe the same SHDF dataset and T-AVFD framework. Their sections, equations, tables, figures, references, and Appendix A support reliable comparison; the appendices are identical.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection experiments, robustness tests, and ablations in Section 5, plus generator user ratings and extended experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains the original detection, robustness, ablation, and user-study results in Section 5 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: The facial authenticity learner, differential weighting module, encoders, losses, and inference procedure are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SHDF, AVLips, FakeAVCeleb, and TalkingHeadBench, with the same talking/singing scenarios, generator-controlled tests, and perturbations. No coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains CViT, EfficientViT, RealForensics, LipFD, AVAD, and AVH-Align. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the training-domain, feature-extractor, robustness, and efficiency comparisons.

E3.justification: No substantive protocol revision is reported. Section 5.1 changes '800 real samples' to 'around 800 real samples' for SHDF, without specifying a different count or selection procedure. The remaining sample counts, splits, metrics, and training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The training-domain analysis, six perturbation tests, generator-controlled experiment, prompt studies, component ablations, and Appendix A.4 sensitivity analyses retain the same questions and evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version provides new repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The user-study averaging procedure involving 20 participants and 30 videos per generator is unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported result entries, rankings, and qualitative findings are retained, including the appendix results. For example, Table 2 reports the same SHDF performance for T-AVFD: 85.7% AP and 80.2% AUC.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 and their mathematical definitions are unchanged, including the contrastive objective, modality weighting, alignment loss, and video-score aggregation. No proofs or formal assumptions are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about introducing SHDF, learning facial authenticity patterns, and generalizing across talking and singing deepfakes.

C2.justification: The domain-shift explanations, interpretations of facial semantics and modulation, and applicability claims are unchanged. Appendix A.5 retains the limitation concerning forgery-source attribution and the same future directions.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 replaces an exact SHDF real-test count of 800 with 'around 800', slightly reducing the precision of the reproducibility information. Implementation details, hardware, resource costs, and reported code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to talking-head datasets and alignment-based detectors are unchanged. No research relationship or novelty claim is revised.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited wording and typography edits, including replacing en dashes with hyphens in 'audio-visual' and 'textual-visual', qualifying the SHDF sample count, and updating the arXiv version/date. Section organization and narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Typography edits produce minor caption and paragraph reflow, notably in Figure 1, Table 4, and Section 5.1. All seven figures and eighteen tables retain their content, structure, and placement; appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: V2 preserves the methods, empirical evidence, claims, and complete appendix. Typography and reflow are cosmetic, while 'around 800' slightly reduces sample-count precision without establishing changed experiments. These limited edits produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
